results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

The intro reader predicted all ten roadmap sections in the spec's order, the three kinds of evidence (Larkfield case, the two providers' documentation, the standard's text) and the plain, bounded tone.
50 of 50 aligned units: each outline summary matches the controlling idea of its spec paragraph, in spec order; the three callouts align to nothing.

Three units marked two_ideas were examined (mechanism ¶3, page ¶3, Questions to Ask ¶2). In each the second summary is a subordinate part of the one idea the spec declares (the fingerprint as a property of the token; what each provider supplies for the two routes; callback plus hand-off in the closing transition paragraph). None holds two controlling ideas.
Every body unit ties to one of S1-S5; the introduction, comparison, Larkfield and conclusion units are context, synthesis or transition for those claims.

Each quotation, the 5 tables and the 4 figures are accompanied by a sentence or caption saying what they show. Note: the four-designs table follows the recommendation paragraph without being referred to; its last column carries the reading.

All other declared boundaries express their relationship and pick up the declared known information, some through the heading or a bold lead-in instead of a full sentence (mechanism, in-practice, when-it-goes-wrong).

results.finding: The introduction opens on a specific puzzling scenario, states the claim and gives a roadmap; none of the listed patterns.
The conclusion sorts what is established, conditional and the author's position, adds no new subtopic or body evidence, and does not end on a rephrased thesis alone.

The author's synthesis states what no single section states (one home for the number, a reference for everyone else; safe and dependent; the screen the design cannot reach) and says what follows: two owned artifacts and the questions to ask.
The closing paragraph returns to the 61,000 stolen numbers and the unsigned line, as callback.to names. Its wording is ruled on under flow_is_followable.

The reader named the remaining exposure (the page around the iframe; a script can overlay the form and copy what is typed), the SAQ A eligibility line in force since 31 March 2025 with its two routes, and the controls (script inventory with reasons, content security policy, removing the tag manager and chat widget).
The reader ordered redirect, iframe fields, raw API; named SAQ A, SAQ A and SAQ D; and said the script condition applies to the iframe and not to the redirect.

results.draft_locus: Stripe and Adyen: Where They Differ ¶1
results.quote: both keep card numbers out of a merchant's systems by the same three moves
results.finding: The third move is confinement in a vault kept apart from the provider's own other systems, which the chapter documents for Stripe and marks as not public and as inference for Adyen; this sentence asserts it for both without citation or marking. Elsewhere the vault statements are cited quotations or marked, and 'Here the public record stops' says where the record ends.
